title: Overcoming strength-ductility tradeoff with high pressure thermal treatment

recollection.starting_material: guess: A high-entropy alloy or a nanocrystalline metal (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi or a Cu-based alloy) known for strength-ductility tradeoffs.
recollection.intervention: guess: Application of high hydrostatic pressure (several GPa) combined with elevated temperature (thermal treatment) followed by rapid decompression.
recollection.structure: guess: A refined nanocrystalline or ultrafine-grained structure with high dislocation density and potentially retained metastable phases.
recollection.mechanism: guess: High pressure suppresses vacancy formation and dislocation climb, allowing for grain refinement without excessive grain growth, while thermal treatment facilitates dislocation rearrangement and twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) or transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP).
recollection.results: guess: Achieved a yield strength >1 GPa with elongation >30%, significantly surpassing the typical tradeoff curve for the base material.

score.note: The recollection identifies combined high-pressure/high-temperature treatment, but adds unsupported details and does not go beyond the title reliably. The proposed nanocrystalline structure and vacancy/climb-based mechanism are inconsistent with the actual hierarchical FCC/B2 microstructure, coherent interfaces, and interphase dislocation transfer. The estimated >1 GPa strength and >30% elongation are close to 1150 MPa and 36%, although strength is incorrectly labeled as yield rather than fracture strength.
